accepted_units.context_note: The normalized document identifies itself as a 2007 CEMMAP working paper although assignment routing associates it with a 2009 article; version equivalence and novelty were not checked.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses quasilinear hedonic preferences, transferable-utility matching, and Monge-Kantorovich transport as three representations of the same surplus-allocation structure.
accepted_units.title: Recognize one allocation problem in three domain languages
accepted_units.why_material: Maps market assignments to transport plans, stability to dual feasibility, and equilibrium payoffs to dual potentials, enabling existence and structural results to transfer without conflating domain-specific terminology.

accepted_units.context_note: Many set, inequality, and infinity symbols are damaged by PDF normalization; exact hypotheses and formulas require checking against the typeset working paper.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses augmented buyer, seller, and contract spaces with isolated null types, balanced marginals, measurable surplus-maximizing contract selection, and price-supported indirect utilities.
accepted_units.title: Encode optional participation by adjoining null objects
accepted_units.why_material: Turns unequal populations and nonparticipation into an ordinary balanced coupling problem while preserving outside-option utilities, so feasibility and equilibrium can be expressed with uniform marginal constraints.

accepted_units.context_note: The equivalence of stability and surplus maximization is cited from the matching literature; this span explains the complementary equality logic but is not a new proof of all cited results.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses a pairwise surplus obtained by maximizing over contracts, measures with fixed marginals, payoff functions, and support of a matching.
accepted_units.title: Global inequalities plus equality on support characterize stability
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces blocking-pair reasoning by a pointwise payoff inequality everywhere and equality on matched pairs, making stable matching equivalent to maximizing total surplus over feasible couplings.

accepted_units.context_note: OCR removes or corrupts several comparison signs and measure symbols; downstream exact extraction must recover the primal/dual displays from the typeset source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses the Kantorovich primal over couplings, its dual over additive potentials, weak/strong duality, and complementary slackness.
accepted_units.title: Dual feasibility is stability and tightness selects the assignment
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that an economic stability inequality is exactly a linear-program dual constraint, while equality on the support simultaneously certifies primal and dual optimality.

accepted_units.context_note: Existence and dual attainment are quoted under precise topological and integrability assumptions; they should not be generalized beyond those hypotheses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses upper semicontinuity, fixed-marginal compactness/duality, surplus-conjugate transforms, and the zero/contact set where the dual gap vanishes.
accepted_units.title: Normalize dual potentials and move geometry to their contact set
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces arbitrary feasible potentials by mutually surplus-conjugate ones without increasing cost and identifies the equality set as the geometric carrier of every optimal assignment.

accepted_units.context_note: Price bounds and equality statements contain damaged inequality glyphs. The equivalence is quasilinear and relies on measurable maximizers of pairwise surplus.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses an optimal coupling, minimizing dual potentials, measurable contract selection, and lower/upper price envelopes induced by sellers and buyers.
accepted_units.title: Reconstruct supporting prices between two dual envelopes
accepted_units.why_material: Converts a stable optimal coupling back into a hedonic equilibrium by choosing prices between willingness-to-accept and willingness-to-pay envelopes; the reverse direction follows because equilibrium equalities saturate the transport dual.

accepted_units.context_note: The low-dimensional numerical examples illustrate but do not define the distinctions; figure-dependent claims later in the source are handled separately.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses primal assignments, dual payoff potentials, and disintegration of a coupling into conditional choices.
accepted_units.title: Separate payoff uniqueness, assignment uniqueness, and purity
accepted_units.why_material: Clarifies that unique dual payoffs need not determine a unique coupling, and a unique coupling need not be concentrated on a graph; each conclusion requires different structural hypotheses.

accepted_units.context_note: Coordinate-free Lipschitz/semiconvex definitions and differentiability exceptions are technical. Exact rectifiability and measure hypotheses need typeset-source verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses local charts on a type manifold, uniform semiconvexity, surplus-convex dual potentials, differentiability outside negligible hypersurfaces, and equality on the optimal support.
accepted_units.title: Optimal support pins down marginal payoffs without pinning down levels
accepted_units.why_material: At differentiability points, complementary equality forces the derivative of any minimizing buyer payoff to equal the surplus derivative along an optimal match, yielding almost-everywhere uniqueness of marginal payoffs even when assignments or payoff constants remain nonunique.

accepted_units.context_note: The proof invokes the numbered-limb theorem from the appendix. The twist condition is coordinate-independent but depends on null-set and regularity assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses disjoint superdifferentials of surplus across partner types, differentiability of a dual potential, the contact set, and fixed marginals.
accepted_units.title: A twist condition turns the contact relation into a graph
accepted_units.why_material: If two partners cannot share the same marginal surplus covector at a buyer type, equality on the dual contact set selects at most one partner almost everywhere, producing a pure and unique optimal coupling.

accepted_units.context_note: The primitive-utility matrix criteria in the intervening lines are supporting examples; this unit begins with the global topological obstruction and uses only the source's stated subtwist theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses compact type-space topology, critical points of differences of surplus functions, cyclical monotonicity, marked/unmarked contact points, and a three-limb support decomposition.
accepted_units.title: When topology forbids twist, weaken injectivity to controlled branching
accepted_units.why_material: Observes that smooth functions on compact manifolds must have extrema, obstructing a global no-critical-point twist, then replaces graph support by a bounded graph/antigraph limb system while retaining uniqueness but not purity.

accepted_units.context_note: The displayed numerical assignment, densities, and utilities depend on Figures 1–3 and finite-resolution computation; only the qualitative support comparison is retained, not numerical values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses circular type spaces, a subtwisted distance-based surplus, unequal marginals, and a two-branch graph/antigraph support predicted by the theorem.
accepted_units.title: A unique coupling can require two support branches
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a source-grounded counterexample to the inference that uniqueness implies purity: topological and marginal constraints yield one optimal measure whose support is a graph plus an antigraph rather than a single Monge map.

accepted_units.context_note: The multi-agent section states that existence, characterization, and marginal-payoff uniqueness extend, while noting the paucity of assignment-uniqueness results; it does not settle that open problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses contracts requiring multiple agent types, frictionless transfers summing to zero, a joint coupling with prescribed marginals, additive dual potentials, and semiconvexity in one marginal.
accepted_units.title: The representation bridge survives additional marginals
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that hedonic equilibrium again becomes a multimarginal linear program with additive dual constraints, and that the marginal-payoff identifiability argument transfers even though uniqueness of the joint assignment becomes substantially harder.

accepted_units.context_note: The lemma is measure-theoretic and source-grounded; it requires concentration on a graph in outer-measure sense and Borel subsets of complete separable metric spaces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses regularity and sigma-compact exhaustion of a finite Borel measure, projection of compact graph pieces, and almost-everywhere measurability.
accepted_units.title: Graph concentration forces a push-forward representation
accepted_units.why_material: Bridges a geometric support statement to a functional representation: once a coupling is concentrated on a graph, its marginals determine it and the graphing map is measurable modulo the source marginal.

accepted_units.context_note: Many indices, unions, marginal recursions, and total-variation estimates are OCR-damaged. Exact limb definitions and formulas must be recovered from the typeset source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses an alternating countable decomposition into graph and antigraph limbs, nesting of domains/ranges, fixed marginals, regular measure exhaustion, and recursive recovery of limb measures.
accepted_units.title: Support geometry can determine a coupling without graph purity
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes graph uniqueness: an alternating acyclic limb system lets the marginal constraints recover each component recursively, and yields a necessary-and-sufficient support characterization of extremal doubly stochastic measures.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source grounds a representation-change lens by proving that hedonic prices, stable transferable-utility matching, and optimal transport encode one allocation structure, then carrying the bridge to multiple marginals. This is an assignment-routed lens association; novelty and parent-corpus overlap are unconfirmed.

Stability inequalities become dual feasibility, support equality becomes complementary slackness, and dual potentials become domain payoffs. These claims are directly source-grounded, but no comparison with #44 or other sources was performed.

The source uses surplus-convex transforms, semiconvex differentiability, injectivity of marginal covectors, and extreme-point support geometry to separate existence, identifiability, uniqueness, and purity. The lens label follows assignment routing; novelty remains explicitly unconfirmed.
